name: AI use readiness review catalog
description: Which assessed controls the AI use readiness review groups, how each relates to AI use of Microsoft 365 data, the organizational review areas, and the vendor statements the review quotes. A VIEW over saved results: nothing here changes a finding or a score. Relationship values: AiSpecific (the setting exists for Copilot or Copilot Studio), DirectAccess (the setting decides what an account, and so Copilot acting as that account, can read), SupportingGovernance (the setting limits sharing over time or the reach of a shortfall but does not itself decide access), General (the setting governs every application alike; the tool does not classify applications as AI).

relationships.AiSpecific: A Copilot or Copilot Studio setting.
relationships.DirectAccess: Decides what an account can read in Microsoft 365, which Microsoft documents as what Copilot can surface for that account.
relationships.SupportingGovernance: Limits sharing over time or the reach of a shortfall; it does not by itself decide access.
relationships.General: Governs every application alike; this tool does not classify applications as AI.

organizational.Area: Approved AI tools and business uses
organizational.Question: Which AI tools and which uses of them are approved, and who decided.
What information may not be entered into an AI tool, and how that rule is made known.
organizational.GeneralWording: The rule for confidential and personal information. If your organization handles regulated data (for example electronic protected health information), state the rule for it separately.
organizational.HipaaWording: The rule for electronic protected health information (ePHI) and other confidential information. This item reflects the HIPAA option selected for this review; the review does not assess HIPAA compliance.

vendorFacts.Statement: Microsoft documents that Microsoft Copilot only surfaces organizational data to which individual users have at least view permissions, and that this includes permissions given to users outside the organization.

Source.Title: Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot

vendorFacts.Statement: Microsoft documents that Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions, that content already overshared can be surfaced to anyone who has access, and that sensitivity labels and DLP help protect individual files.

Source.Title: Data protection and auditing for Microsoft Copilot

vendorFacts.Statement: Microsoft documents that Microsoft Copilot Chat requires an eligible Microsoft 365 subscription and a Microsoft Entra ID account, and that a Microsoft Copilot license is not required for eligible users.

Microsoft documents that web search queries generated by Copilot and Copilot Chat are sent to the Bing search service, which operates separately from Microsoft 365 under different data-handling practices, and that agents' own privacy statements and terms of use decide how they handle organizational data.

Source.Title: Enterprise data protection in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat

vendorFacts.Statement: Microsoft documents that a Copilot Studio agent configured with no authentication can be used by any user who has its link, and that which users in the organization can chat with it cannot then be controlled.

readiness.basis: The gate follows Microsoft's guidance to verify each protection before assigning Copilot licenses. Which controls block is the practice's approved standard (Config/tp-standards.json, CopilotReadinessBlockers), not Microsoft's wording.

blockerReasons.AAD-1.2: Without multifactor authentication, a stolen password gives an attacker everything the user can reach, at Copilot's search speed.
blockerReasons.AAD-1.1: Legacy authentication protocols cannot perform multifactor authentication, so they bypass it.
blockerReasons.SPO-1.1: Broad external sharing widens what is exposed; Copilot surfaces whatever an account can open.
blockerReasons.SPO-1.2: When new links default to anyone-with-the-link, content is overshared without anyone deciding to.
blockerReasons.AAD-6.2: Unrestricted user consent lets any user grant an application access to organizational data.
blockerReasons.AAD-15.1: An application holding tenant-takeover permissions reaches everything with no signed-in user.
blockerReasons.PVW-1.1: Without the unified audit log there is no record of what Copilot was asked or what it referenced.
blockerReasons.PPL-3.5: Copilot interaction auditing is the record an investigation of AI use would need.
blockerReasons.PPL-4.1: An agent open to everyone or to any tenant answers people the organization never approved.
blockerReasons.PPL-4.2: An agent without user authentication answers anyone who can reach it.
